lines: +Prepare the 1.27.0 stable release metadata and document AKS identity binding configuration. The existing release entries remain in CHANGELOG.md.

+- Added support for `WorkloadIdentityCredential` identity binding mode in AKS environments. This feature uses an AKS proxy to handle FIC exchanges on behalf of pods, addressing Entra's limit on federated identity credentials per managed identity. Enable it by constructing `WorkloadIdentityCredential` directly with `enable_azure_proxy=True`. Identity binding mode isn't supported through `DefaultAzureCredential`. ([#43287](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-python/pull/43287), [#44147](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-python/pull/44147))

+- Fixed `AzureDeveloperCliCredential` to correctly parse error messages from Azure Developer CLI v1.23.7 and later, which previously caused raw JSON to surface in `ClientAuthenticationError` instead of the underlying error text. ([#46711](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-python/pull/46711))
+- Fixed persistent token cache isolation on macOS when using custom cache names or CAE-enabled caches. ([#49314](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-python/pull/49314))

- Fixed a regression in 1.26.0 where asynchronous `OnBehalfOfCredential` instances could not reuse access or refresh tokens cached by another instance with the same user assertion. Cache entries are now isolated by user assertion, allowing safe reuse across instances, including with `TokenCachePersistenceOptions`. Existing cache entries without assertion binding require a fresh token exchange. ([#49533](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-python/pull/49533))

+[`WorkloadIdentityCredential`][workload_id_cred_ref] supports [AKS identity bindings](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/aks/identity-bindings), which allow multiple clusters to share a federated identity credential for a user-assigned managed identity.
+After configuring an identity binding and authorizing the pod's Kubernetes service account, construct `WorkloadIdentityCredential` directly with `enable_azure_proxy=True`:

+AKS supplies the pod's identity, projected-token, proxy, SNI, and CA configuration. Identity binding mode isn't supported through `DefaultAzureCredential`. The asynchronous `WorkloadIdentityCredential` in `azure.identity.aio` supports the same option.

Credentials default to authenticating to the Microsoft Entra endpoint for Azure Public Cloud. To access resources in other clouds, such as Azure Government or a private cloud, configure credentials with the `authority` argument. [AzureAuthorityHosts](https://aka.ms/azsdk/python/identity/docs#azure.identity.AzureAuthorityHosts) defines authorities for well-known clouds:

|WorkloadIdentityCredential authentication unavailable. The workload options are not fully configured|The `WorkloadIdentityCredential` requires `client_id`, `tenant_id` and `token_file_path` to authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID.|
  • If using `DefaultAzureCredential` then:
    • Ensure client ID is specified via the `workload_identity_client_id` keyword argument or the `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` env variable.
    • Ensure tenant ID is specified via the `AZURE_TENANT_ID` env variable.
    • Ensure token file path is specified via `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE` env variable.
    • Ensure authority host is specified via `AZURE_AUTHORITY_HOST` env variable.
  • If using `WorkloadIdentityCredential` then:
    • Ensure tenant ID is specified via the `tenant_id` keyword argument or the `AZURE_TENANT_ID` env variable.
    • Ensure client ID is specified via the `client_id` keyword argument or the `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` env variable.
    • Ensure token file path is specified via the `token_file_path` keyword argument or the `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE` environment variable.
  • Consult the [product troubleshooting guide](https://azure.github.io/azure-workload-identity/docs/troubleshooting.html) for other issues.

  • AADSTS700212: No matching federated identity record found for presented assertion audience 'api://AKSIdentityBinding'.
|`WorkloadIdentityCredential` isn't configured to use the identity binding proxy|Set the `enable_azure_proxy` keyword argument to `True` when creating `WorkloadIdentityCredential`. Note that identity binding mode isn't supported when `WorkloadIdentityCredential` is used via `DefaultAzureCredential`. `WorkloadIdentityCredential` should be used directly in this scenario.|

+For asynchronous identity binding requests, the credential uses aiohttp when it supports the `server_hostname` argument (aiohttp 3.9 and later). If aiohttp is missing or lacks this support, the credential falls back to Requests running in an executor thread.

+Identity binding mode forwards `connection_timeout`, `read_timeout`, `connection_data_block_size`, and `use_env_settings` to its transport. It continues to select its own transport and session and uses the AKS-provided SNI and CA configuration; credential constructor options for custom transports, sessions, and TLS settings do not override that configuration.

+Token caching uses the original Microsoft Entra endpoint, not the proxy URL. A path prefix in `AZURE_KUBERNETES_TOKEN_PROXY` therefore doesn't change the tenant used for cache entries or prevent token reuse.
